plan.title: Liver drug treatment vs control: DESeq2 DE + GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: Three treated vs three control liver samples, 3' QuantSeq tag-seq counts from STAR/featureCounts. Because it is a 3' tag library, gene counts do not scale with transcript length, so raw integer counts go into DESeq2 without any length correction or TPM/FPKM step. The plan follows the grounded procedure: sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap) to catch outliers/batch before testing; a minimal low-count pre-filter tuned down for 3'-tag libraries (>=5 counts in >=3 samples, the smallest group size); DESeq2 Wald test with an explicit reference level (control) and named contrast (treated vs control); apeglm shrinkage of the reported log2FC; BH-adjusted p-values with independent filtering at alpha=0.05; and preranked fgsea enrichment on the Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark (staged locally) with Reactome as a confirmatory second pass (also staged locally). The report explicitly states the power limitation of an n=3 design (rule R-0017/R-0094: absence of a gene from the significant list is not evidence of no effect) and gives the standard reproducibility record (session info, package versions, gene-set collection versions).

steps.method: vst(blind), PCA, sample distance heatmap, library sizes
keep gene with >=5 counts in >= smallest group size (3 samples)
raw counts, no length correction (3' tag-seq), explicit reference level = control
fgsea preranked GSEA on Wald statistic, MSigDB Hallmark then Reactome
Summary report with QC, DE tables, enrichment, power caveat
